parts.text:
(a) Simplify
$\sqrt{32}+\sqrt{18}$
giving your answer in the form $a\sqrt{2}$, where $a$ is an integer.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: $\sqrt{32}=4\sqrt{2}$ or $\sqrt{18}=3\sqrt{2}$
B1: $(\sqrt{32}+\sqrt{18}=)$ $7\sqrt{2}$
1st B1: for either surd simplified
2nd B1: for $7\sqrt{2}$ or accept $a=7$. Answer only scores B1B1
NB Common error is $\sqrt{32}+\sqrt{18}=\sqrt{50}=5\sqrt{2}$ this scores B0B0 but can use their "5" in (b) to get M1M1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Simplify
$\frac{\sqrt{32}+\sqrt{18}}{3+\sqrt{2}}$
giving your answer in the form $b\sqrt{2}+c$, where $b$ and $c$ are integers.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $\times\frac{3-\sqrt{2}}{3-\sqrt{2}}$ or $\times\frac{-3+\sqrt{2}}{-3+\sqrt{2}}$ seen
1st M1: for an attempt to multiply by $\frac{3-\sqrt{2}}{3-\sqrt{2}}$ (o.e.) Allow poor use of brackets
dM1: $\left[\frac{\sqrt{32}+\sqrt{18}}{3+\sqrt{2}}\times\frac{3-\sqrt{2}}{3-\sqrt{2}}=\right] \frac{a\sqrt{2}(3-\sqrt{2})}{[9-2]} \to \frac{3a\sqrt{2}-2a}{[9-2]}$ (or better)
2nd dM1: for using $a\sqrt{2}$ to correctly obtain a numerator of the form $p+q\sqrt{2}$ where $p$ and $q$ are non-zero integers. Allow arithmetic slips e.g. $21\sqrt{2}-28$ or $3\sqrt{2}\times\sqrt{2}=3$. Follow through their $a=7$ or a new value found in (b). Ignore denominator. Allow use of letter $a$. Dependent on 1st M1. So $3\sqrt{32}-\sqrt{64}+3\sqrt{8}-\sqrt{36}$ is M0 until they reduce to $p+q\sqrt{2}$
A1, A1: $=3\sqrt{2},-2$
1st A1: for $3\sqrt{2}$ or accept $b=3$ from correct working
2nd A1: for $-2$ or accept $c=-2$ from correct working
ALT: $(b\sqrt{2}+c)(3+\sqrt{2})=7\sqrt{2}$ leading to: $3b+c=7$, $3c+2b=0$ (M1), e.g. $3(7-3b)+2b=0$ (o.e.) (dM1) — Simultaneous Equations alternative: 1st M1 for $(b\sqrt{2}+c)(3+\sqrt{2})=7\sqrt{2}$ and forming 2 simultaneous equations. Ft their $a=7$. 2nd dM1 for solving their simultaneous equations: reducing to a linear equation in one variable

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: for reducing to the form $px>q$ with one of $p$ or $q$ correct. Using $px=q$ is M0 unless $>$ appears later on
A1: $x>4$ only
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $5x>20$ M1

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
$x^2-4x-12=0$
$(x+2)(x-6)[=0]$ M1
$x=6,-2$ A1
$x<-2, x>6$ M1, A1ft
1st M1: for multiplying out and attempting to solve a 3TQ with at least $\pm 4x$ or $\pm 12$. See General Principles for definitions of "attempt to solve"
1st A1: for $6$ and $-2$ seen. Allow $x>6, x>-2$ etc to score this mark. Values may be on a sketch.
2nd M1: for choosing the "outside region" for their critical values. Do not award simply for a diagram or table – they must have chosen their "outside" regions
2nd A1ft: follow through their 2 distinct critical values. Allow "," "or" or a "blank" between answers. Use of "and" is M1A0 i.e. loses the final A1
$-2>x>6$ scores M1A0 i.e. loses the final A1 but apply ISW if $x>6, x<-2$ has been seen. Accept $(-\infty,-2)\cup(6,\infty)$ (o.e)
Use of $\leqslant$ instead of $<$ (or $\geqslant$ instead of $>$) loses the final A mark in (b) unless A mark was lost in (a) for $x\geqslant 4$ in which case allow it here.

questions.stem:
A sequence $x_1,x_2,x_3,\ldots$ is defined by
$x_1=1$
$x_{n+1}=ax_n+5, \quad n\geqslant 1$
where $a$ is a constant.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Write down an expression for $x_2$ in terms of $a$.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: $(x_2=)$ $a+5$ B1: accept $a1+5$ or $1\times a+5$ (etc)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Show that $x_3=a^2+5a+5$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
$(x_3)=a"(a+5)"+5$ M1
$=a^2+5a+5$ (*) A1cso
M1: must see $a($ their $x_2)+5$
A1cso: must have seen $a(a[1]+5)+5$ (etc or better). Must have both brackets (....) and no incorrect working seen

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Given that $x_3=41$
(c) find the possible values of $a$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
$41=a^2+5a+5 \Rightarrow a^2+5a-36(=0)$ or $36=a^2+5a$ M1
$(a+9)(a-4)=0$ M1
$a=4$ or $-9$ A1
1st M1: for forming a suitable equation using $x_3$ and 41 and an attempt to collect like terms and reduce to 3TQ (o.e.) Allow one error in sign. Accept for example $a^2+5a+46(=0)$. If completing the square should get to $(a\pm\frac{5}{2})^2=36+\frac{25}{4}$
2nd M1: Attempting to solve their relevant 3TQ (see General Principles)
A1: for both $4$ and $-9$ seen. If $a=4$ and $-9$ is followed by $-9<a<4$ apply ISW. No working or trial and improvement leading to both answers scores 3/3 but no marks for only one answer. Allow use of other letters instead of $a$

questions.stem: The curve $C$ has equation $y=x(5-x)$ and the line $L$ has equation $2y=5x+4$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Use algebra to show that $C$ and $L$ do not intersect.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
$x(5-x)=\frac{1}{2}(5x+4)$ (o.e.) M1
$2x^2-5x+4(=0)$ (o.e.) e.g. $x^2-2.5x+2(=0)$ A1
$b^2-4ac=(-5)^2-4\times 2\times 4$ M1
$=25-32<0$, so no roots or no intersections or no solutions A1
1st M1: for forming a suitable equation in one variable
1st A1: for a correct 3TQ equation. Allow missing "$=0$" Accept $2x^2+4=5x$ etc
2nd M1: for an attempt to evaluate discriminant for their 3TQ. Allow for $b^2>4ac$ or $b^2<4ac$. Allow if it is part of a solution using the formula e.g. $(x=)\frac{5\pm\sqrt{25-32}}{4}$. Correct formula quoted and some correct substitution or a correct expression. False factorising is M0
2nd A1: for correct evaluation of discriminant for a correct 3TQ e.g. $25-32$ (or better) and a comment indicating no roots or equivalent. For contradictory statements score A0
ALT: 2nd M1 for attempt at completing the square $a\left[(x\pm\frac{b}{2a})^2-q\right]+c$; 2nd A1 for $(x-\frac{5}{4})^2=-\frac{7}{16}$ and a suitable comment

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) In the space on page 11, sketch $C$ and $L$ on the same diagram, showing the coordinates of the points at which $C$ and $L$ meet the axes.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
Curve: $\cap$ shape and passing through $(0,0)$ B1
$\cap$ shape and passing through $(5,0)$ B1
Line: +ve gradient and no intersections with $C$. If no $C$ drawn score B0 B1
Line passing through $(0,2)$ and $(-0.8,0)$ marked on axes B1
Coordinates must be seen on the diagram. Do not award if only in the body of the script. "Passing through" means not stopping at and not touching. Allow $(0,x)$ and $(y,0)$ if marked on the correct places on the correct axis.
1st B1: for correct shape and passing through origin. Can be assumed if it passes through the intersection of axes
2nd B1: for correct shape and 5 marked on x-axis
SC: for $\cap$ shape stopping at both $(5,0)$ and $(0,0)$ award B0B1
3rd B1: for a line of positive gradient that (if extended) has no intersection with their C (possibly extended). Must have both graphs on same axes for this mark. If no C given score B0
4th B1: for straight line passing through $-0.8$ on x-axis and $2$ on y-axis. Accept exact fraction equivalents to $-0.8$ or $2$ (e.g. $\frac{4}{2}$)

questions.stem:
Figure 1 shows the lines $l_1$ and $l_2$, which meet the axes at points $A$, $B$ and $C$.
The line $l_1$ has equation $2x-3y+12=0$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the gradient of $l_1$.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
$(m=)\frac{2}{3}$ (or exact equivalent) B1
B1: for $\frac{2}{3}$ seen. Do not award for $\frac{2}{3}x$ and must be in part (a)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The line $l_1$ crosses the $x$-axis at the point $A$ and the $y$-axis at the point $B$, as shown in Figure 1.
The line $l_2$ is perpendicular to $l_1$ and passes through $B$.
(b) Find an equation of $l_2$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
B: $(0,4)$ [award when first seen – may be in (c)] B1
Gradient: $\frac{-1}{m}=-\frac{3}{2}$ M1
$y-4=-\frac{3x}{2}$ or equiv. e.g. $\left(y=-\frac{3x}{2}+4, \; 3x+2y-8=0\right)$ A1
B1: for coordinates of B. Accept 4 marked on y-axis (clearly labelled)
M1: for use of perpendicular gradient rule. Follow through their value for m
A1: for a correct equation (any form, need not be simplified). Answer only 3/3

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The line $l_2$ crosses the $x$-axis at the point $C$.
(c) Find the area of triangle $ABC$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
A: $(-6,0)$ [award when first seen – may be in (b)] B1
C: $\frac{3x}{2}=4 \Rightarrow x=\frac{8}{3}$ [award when first seen – may be in (b)] B1ft
Area: Using $\frac{1}{2}(x_C-x_A)y_B$ M1
$=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{8}{3}+6\right)4=\frac{52}{3}\left(=17\frac{1}{3}\right)$ A1cso
1st B1: for the coordinates of A (clearly labelled). Accept $-6$ marked on x-axis
2nd B1ft: for the coordinates of C (clearly labelled) or $AC=\frac{26}{3}$. Accept $x=\frac{8}{3}$ marked on x-axis. Follow through from $l_2$ if $>0$
M1: for an expression for the area of the triangle (all lengths $>0$). Ft their $4, -6$ and $\frac{8}{3}$
A1cso: for $\frac{52}{3}$ or exact equivalent seen but must be a single fraction or $17\frac{1}{3}$ or $17\frac{2}{6}$ etc. $17\frac{1}{3}$ on its own can only score full marks if A, B and C are all correct.
ALT (Use of similar triangles): $BC=\frac{4}{6}\sqrt{52}$ (from similar triangles) (or possibly using C) 2nd B1ft; Area: Using $\frac{1}{2}(AB\times BC)$ M1, N.B. $AB=\sqrt{6^2+4^2}=\sqrt{52}$; $=\frac{1}{2}\times\sqrt{52}\times\left(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{52}\right)=\frac{52}{3}\left(=17\frac{1}{3}\right)$ A1
ALT (Use of Det): 2nd M1 must get as far as: $\frac{1}{2}|x_A\times y_B-x_C\times y_B|$

parts.text:
A curve with equation $y=\mathrm{f}(x)$ passes through the point $(2,10)$. Given that
$\mathrm{f}'(x)=3x^2-3x+5$
find the value of $\mathrm{f}(1)$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
$[\mathrm{f}(x)=]\frac{3x^3}{3}-\frac{3x^2}{2}+5x[+c]$ or $\left\{x^3-\frac{3}{2}x^2+5x(+c)\right\}$ M1A1
$10=8-6+10+c$ M1
$c=-2$ A1
$\mathrm{f}(1)=1-\frac{3}{2}+5$ "$-2$" $=\frac{5}{2}$ (o.e.) A1ft
1st M1: for attempt to integrate $x^n\to x^{n+1}$
1st A1: all correct, possibly unsimplified. Ignore $+c$ here.

2nd A1: for $c=-2$
3rd A1ft: for $\frac{9}{2}+c$ Follow through their numerical c ($\neq 0$). This mark is dependent on 1st M1 and 1st A1 only.

questions.stem:
A company offers two salary schemes for a 10-year period, Year 1 to Year 10 inclusive.
Scheme 1: Salary in Year 1 is £$P$.
Salary increases by £$(2T)$ each year, forming an arithmetic sequence.
Scheme 2: Salary in Year 1 is £$(P+1800)$.
Salary increases by £$T$ each year, forming an arithmetic sequence.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that the total earned under Salary Scheme 1 for the 10-year period is
£$(10P+90T)$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
$S_{10}=\frac{10}{2}[2P+9\times 2T]$ or $\frac{10}{2}(P+[P+18T])$ M1
e.g. $5[2P+18T]=(£)(10P+90T)$ or (£)$10P+90T$ (*) A1cso
M1: for identifying $a=P$ or $d=2T$ and attempt at $S_{10}$. Using $n=10$ and one of a or d correct. Must see evidence for M mark, at least one line before the answer.
A1cso: for simplifying to given answer. No incorrect working seen. Do not penalise missing end bracket in working eg $5(2P+18T)$
List: M1A1 for a full list seen (with $+$ signs or written in columns) and no incorrect working seen. Any missing terms is M0A0

parts.label: b
parts.text:
For the 10-year period, the total earned is the same for both salary schemes.
(b) Find the value of $T$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
Scheme 2: $S_{10}=\frac{10}{2}[2(P+1800)+9T]=\{10P+18000+45T\}$ M1A1
$10P+90T=10P+18000+45T$ M1
$90T=18000+45T$
$T=400$ (only) A1
1st M1: for attempting $S_{10}$ for scheme 2 (allow missing (...) brackets e.g. $2P+1800+9T$) Using $n=10$ and at least one of a or d correct.
1st A1: for a correct expression for $S_{10}$ using scheme 2 (needn't be multiplied out). Allow M1A1 if they reach $10P+18000+45T$ with no incorrect working seen. $10P+18000+45T$ with no working is M1A1
2nd M1: for forming an equation using the two sums that would enable P to be eliminated. Follow through their expressions provided P would disappear.
2nd A1: for $T=400$ Answer only (4/4)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
For this value of $T$, the salary in Year 10 under Salary Scheme 2 is £29 850
(c) Find the value of $P$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
Scheme 2, Year 10 salary: $[a+(n-1)d=](P+1800)+9T$ B1ft
$P+1800+"3600"=29850$ M1
$P=(£)24450$ A1
B1: for using $u_{10}$ for scheme 2. Can be $9T$ or follow through their value of T
M1: for forming an equation based on $u_{10}$ for scheme 2 and using $29850$ and their value of T
A1: for $24450$ seen. Answer only (3/3)
MR: If they misread scheme 2 as scheme 1 in part (c) apply MR rule and award B0M1A0 max for an equation based on $u_{10}$ for scheme 1 and using $29850$ and their value of T

questions.stem:
Figure 2 shows a sketch of the curve $C$ with equation
$y=2-\frac{1}{x}, \quad x\neq 0$
The curve crosses the $x$-axis at the point $A$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the coordinates of $A$.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\left(\frac{1}{2},0\right)$ B1
B1: accept $x=\frac{1}{2}$ if evidence that $y=0$ has been used. Can be written on graph. Use ISW

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Show that the equation of the normal to $C$ at $A$ can be written as
$2x+8y-1=0$
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\frac{dy}{dx}=x^{-2}$ M1A1
At $x=\frac{1}{2}$, $\frac{dy}{dx}=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{-2}=4$ $(=m)$ A1
Gradient of normal $=-\frac{1}{m}$ $\left(=-\frac{1}{4}\right)$ M1
Equation of normal: $y-0=-\frac{1}{4}\left(x-\frac{1}{2}\right)$ M1
$2x+8y-1=0$ (*) A1cso
1st M1: for $kx^{-2}$ even if the '2' is not differentiated to zero. If no evidence of $\frac{dy}{dx}$ seen then 0/6
1st A1: for $x^{-2}$ (o.e.) only
2nd A1: for using $x=0.5$ to get $m=4$ (correctly) (or $m=1/0.25$). To score final A1cso must see at least one intermediate equation for the line after $m=4$
2nd M1: for using the perpendicular gradient rule on their m coming from their $\frac{dy}{dx}$. Their m must be a value not a letter.
3rd M1: for using a changed gradient (based on y') and their A to find equation of line
3rd A1cso: for reaching printed answer with no incorrect working seen. Accept $2x+8y=1$ or equivalent equations with $\pm 2x$ and $\pm 8y$

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The normal to $C$ at $A$ meets $C$ again at the point $B$, as shown in Figure 2.
(c) Find the coordinates of $B$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
$2-\frac{1}{x}=-\frac{1}{4}x+\frac{1}{8}$ M1
$[=2x^2+15x-8=0]$ or $[8y^2-17y=0]$ M1
$(2x-1)(x+8)=0$ leading to $x=\ldots$
$x=\left[\frac{1}{2}\right]$ or $-8$ A1
$y=\frac{17}{8}$ (or exact equivalent) A1ft
Trial and improvement requires sight of first equation.
1st M1: for attempt to form a suitable equation in one variable. Do not penalise poor use of brackets etc.
2nd M1: for simplifying their equation to a 3TQ and attempting to solve. May be $\Rightarrow$ by $x=-8$
1st A1: for $x=-8$ (ignore a second value). If found y first allow ft for x if $x<0$
2nd A1ft: for $y=\frac{17}{8}$ Follow through their x value in line or curve provided answer is $>0$. This second A1 is dependent on both M marks
